hints: Look at each row as an electrophilic addition to the C=C bond in propene, so ask where each part of the reagent adds.
Remember Markovnikov's rule for unsymmetrical reagents like HCl and H2O, the H adds to the carbon with more H atoms already.
Check which product names put the functional group on carbon 2 versus carbon 1, and which reagent cannot give that type of product at all.
walkthrough:
**Recall what propene does**

Propene is an unsymmetrical alkene, so it undergoes electrophilic addition. The key question is always which carbon gets which part.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{X-Y} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHX-CH}_2\text{Y or CH}_3\text{CHY-CH}_2\text{X}$$

**Apply Markovnikov's rule**

For H-X reagents like HCl and H-OH (steam with acid catalyst), H+ adds first to make the more stable secondary carbocation on carbon 2. The negative part then joins carbon 2.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHCl-CH}_3$$

**Check the oxidation and halogen-water reactions**

Cold dilute $\text{MnO}_4^-$ adds two OH groups across the double bond to give a 1,2-diol, not a 1,3-diol. Aqueous $\text{Br}_2$ gives a bromohydrin (bromo-alcohol), not just a bromoalkane.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + [\text{O}] + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Match to the table**

Only hydrogen chloride giving 2-chloropropane fits Markovnikov addition correctly. Steam should give propan-2-ol, not propan-1-ol.

options.A: Incorrect. Bromine in water does not give 2-bromopropane. Dry $\text{Br}_2$ gives 1,2-dibromopropane and aqueous $\text{Br}_2$ gives a bromohydrin such as 1-bromo-propan-2-ol. 2-bromopropane is the product with HBr, not aqueous bromine.
options.B: Incorrect. Cold acidified aqueous $\text{KMnO}_4$ hydroxylates the double bond to form adjacent OH groups. For propene this is propane-1,2-diol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$. Propane-1,3-diol would need OH groups on carbons 1 and 3, which cannot form by direct addition across C1=C2.
options.C: Correct. HCl adds by Markovnikov electrophilic addition. H+ adds to C1 to give the more stable secondary carbocation on C2, then $\text{Cl}^-$ bonds to C2 to give 2-chloropropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHClCH}_3$, as the main product.
options.D: Incorrect. Steam with hot concentrated $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ catalyst hydrates propene by Markovnikov addition, so OH adds to the more substituted carbon 2. The product is propan-2-ol, not propan-1-ol. Propan-1-ol would be anti-Markovnikov.
